result:
There is a fragile, unnamed hour just before the city wakes, when the world belongs entirely to the quiet. Outside the window, the sky turns the color of bruised slate, slowly fading into a pale, watery blue. Streetlights buzz with a sleepy hum, casting long, amber halos onto the empty pavement. In this suspension of time, the pressing demands of yesterday have dissolved, and the anxieties of tomorrow haven’t yet found their footing.

I listen to the kettle whistle its soft, rising crescendo. The aroma of freshly ground coffee blooms into the cool kitchen air: dark, earthy, and reassuring. It feels like an anchor in an otherwise restless existence. Holding the warm ceramic mug between two cold palms, I watch a solitary cyclist drift down the quiet avenue, moving through the mist like a ghost on two wheels. Where are they going? Perhaps to an early shift, perhaps returning from an overnight vigil, or maybe just chasing the same peace I am currently savoring.

We spend so much of our lives rushing toward the next milestone, checking off boxes, and filling every silence with noise and endless digital notifications. But these stolen, solitary moments remind us that existence doesn't always need a grand purpose to be meaningful. Sometimes, it is enough simply to witness the dawn breaking over the rooftops, to feel the steam gently brush against your cold eyelashes, and to breathe in a sleeping world that is, for just a few minutes longer, entirely still and full of possibilities.
